## Question 4.1: Web scraping and data extraction

### Use case: Analysing book prices and ratings
This use case investigates the prices and ratings of books listed on
Books to Scrape. Book details are extracted from the website and
organised into an R data frame. The data will then be cleaned and
exported for analysis in PostgreSQL.

Books to Scrape is a demonstration website designed for scraping
practice. Its prices and ratings are simulated, so the results
describe this demonstration dataset rather than real book prices
or reader reviews.

```{r}
# Install packages 
packages <- c("rvest", "dplyr", "stringr")

for (package in packages) {
  if (!requireNamespace(package, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(package)
  }
}

# Load the packages
library(rvest)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
```

```{r}
catalogue_url <- "https://books.toscrape.com/"
catalogue_page <- read_html(catalogue_url)

# Select each book listing on the page
book_listings <- catalogue_page |>
  html_elements("article.product_pod")

# Extract raw information from each listing
raw_books <- data.frame(
  title = book_listings |>
    html_element("h3 a") |>
    html_attr("title"),

  price_raw = book_listings |>
    html_element(".price_color") |>
    html_text(),

  rating_raw = book_listings |>
    html_element("p.star-rating") |>
    html_attr("class"),

  availability_raw = book_listings |>
    html_element(".availability") |>
    html_text(),

  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Check the number of records and inspect raw data
nrow(raw_books)
raw_books
```
```{r}
# Shows the first five records and all four columns
print(head(raw_books, 5))

# Count missing values in each column
colSums(is.na(raw_books))

# Check for blank values in each column
colSums(sapply(raw_books, function(column) {
  is.na(column) | trimws(column) == ""
}))
```
```{r}
# I'm extracting the price from the text so I can analyse it as a number
raw_books$price_numeric <- as.numeric(
  str_extract(raw_books$price_raw, "[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+")
)

# I'm finding the rating word inside each book's HTML class
raw_books$rating_word <- str_extract(
  raw_books$rating_raw,
  "One|Two|Three|Four|Five"
)

# I'm converting the rating words into numbers from 1 to 5
rating_values <- c(
  One = 1,
  Two = 2,
  Three = 3,
  Four = 4,
  Five = 5
)

raw_books$rating_numeric <- unname(
  rating_values[raw_books$rating_word]
)

# I'm checking the original values alongside the extracted values
print(head(raw_books[, c(
  "title",
  "price_raw",
  "price_numeric",
  "rating_raw",
  "rating_numeric"
)], 5))
```
## Regex extraction
Regular expressions were used to extract the numerical price and the rating word from each book listing. The price was converted from text containing a pound symbol into a numeric value, while the rating word was converted into a number between one and five. The original values were retained so that they could be compared with the extracted values.


## Question 4.2: Data cleaning and export
The scraped book data was cleaned to prepare it for database analysis.
This included removing unnecessary whitespace, checking for duplicate
records and examining missing or invalid values.

```{r}
# I'm creating a separate data frame for the cleaned book data
clean_books <- data.frame(
  title = str_squish(raw_books$title),
  price_gbp = raw_books$price_numeric,
  rating = raw_books$rating_numeric,
  availability = str_squish(raw_books$availability_raw),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# I'm checking for duplicate records before removing them
duplicate_count <- sum(duplicated(clean_books))
cat("Number of duplicate records:", duplicate_count, "\n")

# I'm removing exact duplicate rows if there are any
clean_books <- distinct(clean_books)

# I'm checking for missing values in the cleaned columns
colSums(is.na(clean_books))

# I'm checking that prices and ratings are within sensible ranges
cat("Invalid prices:", sum(clean_books$price_gbp <= 0, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Invalid ratings:", sum(!clean_books$rating %in% 1:5 &
                              !is.na(clean_books$rating)), "\n")

# I'm previewing the cleaned records
head(clean_books)
```
```{r}
# I'm checking the quality of the cleaned dataset
cat("Number of cleaned records:", nrow(clean_books), "\n")
cat("Duplicate records found:", duplicate_count, "\n\n")

cat("Missing values in each column:\n")
print(colSums(is.na(clean_books)))

cat("\nInvalid prices:",
    sum(clean_books$price_gbp <= 0, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

cat("Invalid ratings:",
    sum(!clean_books$rating %in% 1:5 & !is.na(clean_books$rating)),
    "\n")
```
```{r}
# I'm making a separate copy to demonstrate missing-value imputation
imputation_demo <- clean_books

# I'm deliberately hiding one price for this demonstration
imputation_demo$price_gbp[1] <- NA

# I'm calculating the median from the remaining available prices
median_price <- median(imputation_demo$price_gbp, na.rm = TRUE)

# I'm replacing the missing price with the median
imputation_demo$price_gbp[is.na(imputation_demo$price_gbp)] <- median_price

# I'm comparing the original price with the imputed estimate
data.frame(
  book = clean_books$title[1],
  original_price = clean_books$price_gbp[1],
  imputed_price = imputation_demo$price_gbp[1]
)
```
### Missing-value imputation
No missing values were found in the cleaned scraped dataset. To
demonstrate an appropriate imputation technique, a separate copy of
the data was created and one price was deliberately set to missing.
The missing price was replaced with the median of the remaining
prices. This was a demonstration only; the original cleaned dataset
retained its observed prices for export and analysis.

```{r}
# I'm exporting the cleaned book data for PostgreSQL
write.csv(
  clean_books,
  file = "clean_books.csv",
  row.names = FALSE,
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
)

# I'm checking where the CSV was saved
normalizePath("clean_books.csv")
```

### Exporting the cleaned data
The cleaned dataset was exported as a CSV file for import into
PostgreSQL. It contains the observed prices and ratings from the
scraped records. The imputation demonstration was performed separately
and did not alter the exported data.
